purpose: The approved factual alternative to customer testimonials, per account. Every item names what backs it, and declares that it makes no customer and no metric claim.
binding_decision: No supplied customer testimonial quotation is approved for production. Four accounts supply unverified or self-declared placeholder quotations (UI05-CONTENT-001); three supply no testimonials section at all (UI05-CONTENT-002). All eight pages carry a factual alternative instead. No source text was deleted or rewritten.

accounts.heading: Built for accountable service operations
accounts.intro: This account owns the business record. These are the controls that come with it — product capability and security architecture, not customer claims.

items.title: Your business is its own tenant
items.detail: Every record belongs to one merchant. Another merchant cannot read, infer, edit, export or enumerate it.
items.source_reference: cross-tenant read/write denial across every tenant-owned model

items.title: No passwords to lose
items.detail: Sign-in is a single-use Magic Link, hashed at rest, valid for fifteen minutes and bound to the account address it was requested from.
items.source_reference: token hashing, single-use consume and expiry

items.title: Access follows the role, not the person
items.detail: Branch, HR, Finance, Front Office, Personnel and Audit each see the work their role owns, and nothing beyond it.

items.title: Servana never touches client money
items.detail: Clients pay your business offline. Servana records the method, amount, reference and validation state so the record is reviewable.
items.source_reference: §6 Features Section — "Invoices and offline payment records"

accounts.heading: Independence you can check
accounts.intro: An audit account is only worth having if its independence is structural. These are the mechanisms that make it so — implemented behaviour, not customer evidence.

items.title: Read-only is enforced, not agreed
items.detail: The audit account cannot edit clients, services, invoices, payments, receipts, users, queues or commissions. The API refuses, not the interface.
items.source_reference: mutation denial across every audited surface

items.title: The record is append-only and chained
items.detail: Audit entries cannot be updated or deleted, and each is hash-chained to the one before it, so a silent edit would break the chain.

items.title: An export is scoped to your own business
items.detail: Audit exports are generated within the merchant tenant and are not readable from another one.

items.title: Review does not slow the floor down
items.detail: Audit reads the record after the fact. It sits outside the queue, the till and the receipt, so reviewing never blocks the people serving clients.
items.source_reference: §11 Security / Trust Section — "designed for oversight, not control"

accounts.heading: Designed for controlled branch operations
accounts.intro: A branch account is scoped to its branch by design. These are the controls that keep it that way — implemented behaviour, not customer evidence.

items.title: Branch scope is enforced by the server
items.detail: A branch account reaches its own branch. Branch assignment is re-checked on every protected request, never inferred from the page you are on.

items.title: The branch owns its service catalogue and its day
items.detail: Services, pricing and the operating calendar belong to the branch. Queue, appointment and payment records stay readable to it.
items.source_reference: §6 Features Section — service catalogue and branch day

items.title: Recording a payment is not validating one
items.detail: The branch sees payment records. Validating a payment and issuing a receipt stay with Finance, which is what keeps the receipt trustworthy.
items.source_reference: branch cannot validate payments or issue receipts

items.title: Access is checked, not assumed
items.detail: User status, role status, merchant assignment, branch assignment and Magic Link rules are all evaluated before a branch record is returned.

accounts.heading: Operational confidence in the money record
accounts.intro: Finance is the validating role, so the controls around it are the point. These are implemented behaviours, not customer claims.

items.title: A receipt cannot exist before validation
items.detail: Receipt issuance is driven by validation, and the rule is enforced in the database rather than only in application code.

items.title: Receipt and invoice numbers are unique by construction
items.detail: Numbering is allocated under a database uniqueness guarantee, so two concurrent issues cannot produce the same number.

items.title: Recording and validating are different hands
items.detail: Front Office records what a client paid. Finance decides whether that record is accurate. Neither role can do both.

items.title: Servana takes no client payment
items.detail: Clients pay the business offline by cash, M-Pesa, bank transfer, card terminal, voucher or split payment. Servana holds the record, not the money.

accounts.heading: Built for accountable service at the front desk
accounts.intro: The front desk touches clients, queues and money records, so its limits matter as much as its tools. These are implemented behaviours, not customer claims.

items.title: Record a payment, never validate one
items.detail: Front Office captures the method, amount and reference. Confirming it and issuing the receipt belong to Finance.
items.source_reference: front-office cannot validate payments or issue receipts

items.title: Two clients cannot hold the same slot
items.detail: Overlapping appointments for one person are rejected by a database exclusion constraint, not only by a form check.

items.title: A duplicate payment reference is caught
items.detail: A reference already recorded against another payment is flagged for review instead of being quietly accepted twice.

items.title: Client records stay inside the business
items.detail: Client data belongs to the merchant tenant. It is not readable by another business, and there is no contact-export capability anywhere in the product.
items.source_reference: contact-export prohibition — no field, no endpoint, no screen

accounts.heading: Trust through clear responsibility
accounts.intro: The commitments below are how that is actually enforced — implemented behaviour, not customer evidence.

items.title: HR works within its own branch
items.detail: Staff records, roles, availability and compensation setup are scoped to the branch HR is assigned to.

items.title: HR cannot grant itself more access
items.detail: Permission changes are checked against the role boundary, so an HR user cannot escalate its own or a peer role beyond what the matrix allows.

items.title: Every access change is checked before it applies
items.detail: Whether the user is active, belongs to the correct merchant, holds the right role and may reach the relevant branch is evaluated on each request.

items.title: Staff and client records stay separate concerns
items.detail: HR manages people. It does not export client records or payment details, and no contact-export capability exists for it.
items.source_reference: contact-export prohibition — no field, no endpoint, no screen

accounts.heading: Your work, your record, your limits
accounts.intro: A personnel account is deliberately narrow. These are the boundaries and controls that define it — implemented behaviour, not customer claims.

items.title: You see your own work
items.detail: Queue, appointments, sessions and earnings are scoped to you. The account does not open the wider business to you, and it does not need to.

items.title: Client contact export does not exist
items.detail: There is no field, no endpoint and no screen anywhere in Servana that exports personnel client contacts. It is a product-wide prohibition, not a permission you have not been given.
items.source_reference: contact-export prohibition — no field, no endpoint, no screen

items.title: Commission comes from recorded work
items.detail: Earned and pending commission are derived from completed, validated service records, so the figure has something behind it.

items.title: Sign-in is a link, not a password
items.detail: You log in with a single-use Magic Link sent to the email your business activated. Nothing to remember, nothing to leak.
items.source_reference: token hashing, single-use consume and expiry

accounts.heading: Security and accountability
accounts.intro: This account governs the platform. What follows is the architecture that governs it in turn — implemented controls, not customer evidence.

items.title: Merchant data stays separated
items.detail: Every merchant is an isolated tenant. Platform-level reads cross that boundary only through explicit platform services, never through an ordinary query.

items.title: Privileged access requires a second factor
items.detail: The platform account requires MFA enrollment, and sensitive platform changes require a fresh step-up challenge.

items.title: The audit record cannot be rewritten
items.detail: Audit entries are append-only and hash-chained, and the chain is verified on a schedule rather than on request.

items.title: Oversight without interference
items.detail: Platform governance reviews merchant activity; it does not operate a merchant’s day. Merchants keep their own clients, queues, invoices and receipts.
